description: The Canadian Disaster Database records more than 1,000 natural, technological and conflict disasters (excluding war) since 1900 that directly affected Canadians at home or abroad. Events are included when they killed 10 or more people, affected 100 or more, led to an appeal for assistance, were historically significant or caused damage the community could not recover from alone; each record gives where and when the disaster occurred, injuries, evacuations, fatalities and an estimate of costs. It is maintained by Public Safety Canada from federal, provincial and territorial, non-governmental and public sources, and is reviewed and updated periodically. An extract to 2022 is available free as XLSX in English and French on the Open Government Portal under the Open Government Licence – Canada, alongside an online search tool. Caveats: Public Safety Canada warns that cost data lack a standard, recent figures are preliminary, and the database may not suit comparative analysis. It gives Canadian historical event and loss records for hazard frequency and impact analysis of infrastructure; a related record is EM-DAT.
